Reading the HPD record

What the violation classes mean

HPD uses three severity classes under the NYC Housing Maintenance Code. The class describes how serious the cited condition is.

A

Class A · Non-hazardous

A lower-severity maintenance condition that must be corrected but is not classified as an immediate health or safety hazard.

B

Class B · Hazardous

A condition that presents a health or safety risk and is treated as more urgent than a Class A violation.

C

Class C · Immediately hazardous

The most serious category, used for conditions requiring urgent correction because they may immediately threaten health or safety.

RI

Rent-impairing indicator

A condition in a multiple dwelling that is, or may become if not promptly corrected, a fire hazard or a serious threat to occupants’ life, health, or safety.

Source: NYC HPD Housing Maintenance Code Violations dataset, which defines the RentImpairing field by reference to New York State Multiple Dwelling Law § 302. The full property profile reports open violations returned by NYC HPD at the time of the request. Rent-impairing is a separate legal indicator, not a fourth violation class. Classification indicates severity; review the individual description and HPD Online record for the specific condition and current status.

Context beyond the raw violation count

Five housing-condition covariates

Select a property to load building-level and neighborhood context. Counts and rates remain separate; the map does not create a composite landlord, danger, or housing-risk score.

1

Reported complaint burden

HPD-related 311 service requests during the previous 12 months, shown as both a raw count and a rate per 100 residential units.

2

Violation persistence and recurrence

Open violations per 100 units, the earliest open NOV issue date, recent issuance, and repeated Class B or C condition descriptions.

3

Ownership portfolio size

The number of source-matched buildings and residential units linked separately to the HPD corporate owner and managing agent.

4

Executed-eviction pressure

Official executed-eviction records during the previous 12 months and three years. Court filing counts are not included in this release.

5

Neighborhood rent burden and income

ZIP/ZCTA median income, median gross rent, rent burden, severe rent burden, and poverty context from the ACS.

Interpretation: reported complaints may reflect differences in residents’ access to and willingness to use 311. Neighborhood ACS values describe the surrounding ZIP Code Tabulation Area, not the finances or circumstances of an individual tenant.

Methodology

What the map includes

Only properties appearing in the named NYC Rent Guidelines Board/NYS Homes and Community Renewal building lists are mapped. Records are joined by normalized ten-character BBL to PLUTO and HPD public records.

Interpretation warning: HPD corporate owner, managing agent, site manager, individual owner, and joint owner are administrative roles. They are preserved separately and do not independently establish beneficial ownership.
NYC Housing Intelligence · Public data and spatial research project

Methodology and limits

About this map

This map includes only properties appearing in named RGB/HCR rent-stabilized building lists. Inclusion is based on an exact normalized ten-character BBL match.

Important limitation: A building-list match means at least one apartment was registered as rent stabilized. It does not identify the apartment, establish current legal status for every unit, or mean every apartment is stabilized.

PLUTO supplies property characteristics. HPD registration and contact records identify public administrative roles. HPD violations, HPD-related 311 requests, executed-eviction records, and ZIP/ZCTA ACS context are requested when a property is selected. The ACS request is delivered through Census Reporter because the current Census API requires an API key. Ownership portfolio size is calculated from exact role-name matches within the embedded inventory. A failed live request is never interpreted as zero.
